name: Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome with Complement Gene Abnormality

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia evidenced by schistocytes on blood smear and elevated LDH
Thrombocytopenia with platelet count below normal reference range
Acute kidney injury with elevated serum creatinine and reduced glomerular filtration rate
Identification of pathogenic variants in complement regulatory genes (e.g., CFH, CFI, MCP/CD46)
Exclusion of Shiga-toxin producing E. coli infection and other secondary causes of thrombotic microangiopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, acute kidney injury, and exclusion of other causes of thrombotic microangiopathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for complement gene abnormalities supports diagnosis but is not mandatory for initial diagnosis.

searchTerms: anemia from small blood vessel damage
red blood cell destruction in tiny vessels
hemolytic anemia due to microvascular injury
fatigue related to low red blood cells

occasional.symptomName: Neurological manifestations including confusion or seizures
searchTerms: neurological symptoms including altered mental state

occasional.symptomName: Gastrointestinal symptoms such as abdominal pain or diarrhea

searchTerms: body swelling due to fluid retention

occasional.symptomName: Dyspnea secondary to anemia or fluid overload
searchTerms: shortness of breath from anemia or fluid
difficulty breathing due to low red cells or fluid overload
breathlessness caused by anemia or swelling

laboratory: Elevated serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
Low C3 complement levels in some cases
imaging: Renal ultrasound showing normal or enlarged kidneys
Brain MRI in cases with neurological symptoms may show ischemic changes
other: Negative Shiga-toxin assay to exclude typical HUS
Normal ADAMTS13 activity to exclude thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of Shiga-toxin producing E. coli infection
Less severe renal involvement compared to aHUS

redFlags: Neurological deterioration including seizures or coma
